content.comment_body: Hi, I would like to connect five [product_name] units that are about 1km apart. Is it possible to do this by connecting each [product_name] to a 4G modem? If so, what would be the setup process?

Hello, It depends on how much data you want to transfer. There is an example of two [product_name] controllers, each connected with a [product_name] mobile communication module, exchanging data via SMS. [url] This concept can be extended to five stations, but each [product_name] mobile communication module can monitor up to 32 signals. If this meets your needs, it could be a suitable solution. Otherwise, you may require four routers with interconnection (either private or public APN) and can configure a controller-to-controller connection through the communication modules. Kind regards, [user_name]

Using a mobile communication module provides sufficient signal capacity, but opting for a 4G router may be a more cost-effective and flexible approach compared to SMS-based communication. Another idea, is cloud-service communication possible? For example, can you access a signal on another [product_name] via the cloud?

You could use the communication interface module, which is a recent addition and functions as both a switch and a messaging module with SIM card support. It is newly introduced for [company_name] controllers and allows cloud connectivity as well.
That sounds promising. Where can I find information on the communication interface module?
You can download the manual for the [product_name] communication interface module here.
After some research, I'm considering another option. Would it be possible to use [product_name] V[version_no] and AWS? Could parameters be exchanged between various controllers using AWS?
Good afternoon, You may want to check out this video for guidance—it focuses on networking rather than cloud solutions: [product_name] Tips and Tricks - Network project (EN) - YouTube.

Connecting via Ethernet is straightforward, but my question is whether remote networking of controllers through AWS is feasible. This workshop seems to suggest it is possible (see last section): [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are comparing several methods for remotely networking multiple [product_name] devices positioned roughly 1km apart. They discuss hardware and connectivity options such as 4G modems, SMS transmission via communication modules, cloud-based networking (like AWS), and new switch/messaging modules that support cloud integration. Participants seek scalable, cost-effective, and flexible solutions for signal exchange, but there is uncertainty regarding seamless cloud connectivity capabilities and the resources needed for integrating these devices with cloud services.
analysis.user_expectations: Users aim to efficiently network several remotely located [product_name] modules, favoring flexible and affordable solutions. Ideally, they want the ability to transmit signals or parameters through cloud services.
